_comment: Spec consumed by scripts/gen-ci-workflow.py. Lists the test-invocation block of .github/workflows/test.yml. Setup boilerplate (Chez install, idris2 cache+build, MLX/torch install, artifact upload) stays hand-written in the workflow itself; only the steps between the GEN markers are generated from this file. Add a new gate here, run scripts/gen-ci-workflow.py, commit both. The make test-integration-lint-ci-workflow target fails CI if this spec disagrees with the on-disk workflow.

invocations.name: Run idris-transformers unit tests
comment: Pure-Idris test harness for the HF-aligned model package
(packages/idris-transformers/). Type-checks the package + builds
the test executable, then runs it. No backend dependency at this
stage — the package wiring is the gate; HfBert model tests land
alongside HfBert.idr in a later commit.

invocations.name: Run HfBert oracle generator + pytest (Ubuntu)
comment: Drives packages/idris-transformers/scripts/save_oracle.py through
pytest under the pytorch uv venv (carries the transformers dep).
Downloads google/bert_uncased_L-2_H-128_A-2 from HF Hub on each
run, runs forward on the fixed input, asserts the resulting
oracle is shape [128] F32 finite + non-trivial. Ubuntu-only:
ref-setup runs only there in this matrix.

invocations.name: Run HfGpt2 oracle generator + pytest (Ubuntu)
comment: Same shape as the HfBert oracle gate but for sshleifer/tiny-gpt2.
Downloads the checkpoint, runs forward on [15496, 995], asserts
the last-position hidden state is shape [2] (sshleifer/tiny-gpt2
is intentionally degenerate at hidden=2 — exercises the
architectural pieces without burning CI disk). Ubuntu-only.

invocations.name: Run HfBert end-to-end roundtrip (Ubuntu)
comment: The cross-language correctness gate: regenerates the Python
oracle, runs the Idris HfBertInference example (loading the
real Google bert-tiny weights via the HF-aligned HfBert
module), and asserts elementwise agreement within
max-abs-diff 1e-3 on the 128-dim pooled [CLS] output.
Currently passes at 4.1e-4 locally on tape. Ubuntu-only:
depends on the uv venv set up by ref-setup.

invocations.name: Run HfGpt2 end-to-end roundtrip (Ubuntu)
comment: Same gate shape as HfBert but for GPT-2: regenerate the Python
oracle from hf-internal-testing/tiny-random-gpt2, run the Idris
HfGpt2Inference binary, assert the 32-dim last-position hidden
state matches within max-abs-diff 1e-3. Currently passes at
~1e-6 locally on tape. Ubuntu-only: depends on the uv venv.

invocations.name: Run HfBitNet end-to-end roundtrip (Ubuntu, torch)
comment: Cross-language gate: regenerate the Python oracle from
microsoft/bitnet-b1.58-2B-4T, run the Idris HfBitNetInference
binary --dump-logits, assert argmax on the vocab-128256 logit
row matches the HF oracle at max-abs-diff 1.0. BACKEND=torch
because tape F64 on a ~2B-param model OOMs the 14 GB Ubuntu
runner (see Low-priority TODO "Tape F64 large-LM OOM"). BitNet
is not license-gated, so no HF_TOKEN handling needed.

invocations.name: Run HfLlama end-to-end roundtrip (Ubuntu, torch, HF_TOKEN-gated)
comment: Cross-language gate for Llama 3.2 1B. Regenerates the Python
oracle from meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B (license-gated), runs the
Idris HfLlamaInference binary --dump-final-hidden, asserts the
2048-dim last-position hidden state matches the oracle within
max-abs-diff 1.0. Currently passes at 4.96e-05 on torch-mps
and 1.20e-04 on mlx-gpu in local dev runs; the CI torch-cpu
lane carries the same Idris-side numerics through libtorch CPU.
Step skips cleanly when HF_TOKEN is unset in repo/org secrets
(forks without the token won't see a failing step). BACKEND=torch
because tape F64 doesn't fit (~10 GB params + arena vs ~14 GB
runner RAM); see Low-priority TODO "Tape F64 large-LM OOM".

invocations.name: Run HfLlama multi-step generation roundtrip (Ubuntu, torch, HF_TOKEN-gated)
comment: Cross-language gate for Llama 3.2 1B's *generation* path.
The companion `test-e2e-hf-llama-roundtrip` step above tests a
single forward on one fixed token; this step exercises the
full greedy-decode loop: tokenize "The capital of France
is", generate 4 tokens via `genLoop` (no KV cache yet —
bumps to 8+ once KV cache lands), assert the resulting
token-ID sequence matches HF `model.generate(do_sample=
False, use_cache=True)` element-wise. Catches drift in
tokenization, every layer of the forward, argmax, and the
per-step glue that the single-forward gate can't see.
Same HF_TOKEN gating + BACKEND=torch as the sibling step.
Currently more expensive than the single-forward gate (4
forwards on growing sequences); the KV cache landing will
collapse it back to ~constant per step.

invocations.name: Verify GradMode gate (NoGrad loss rejected at compile)
comment: Asserts the type-level gate `nativeTrainStep : ... -> Tensor [] d
WithGrad -> Double` still rejects a `NoGrad` loss. If this step
ever passes the negative test (i.e. the gate compiles a NoGrad
loss), the "inference loss silently no-ops training" bug class
has regressed.

invocations.name: Verify GradMode aliasing rejection (linear freezeNetwork)
comment: Asserts that linear `freezeNetwork` consumes its input — using
the pre-freeze Network reference afterwards must be a compile
error. Prevents the "freeze net, train via original variable
which silently no-ops" footgun.

invocations.name: Verify cross-family lossless-cast gate (DType.Core.LosslessTo)
comment: Asserts LosslessTo refuses a mantissa-shrinking direction
(F32 to BF16). Prevents silent precision-losing mid-graph
casts. Pairs with the positive Test.Lossless suite.

invocations.name: Verify int-overflow lossless-cast gate (#412 F1)
comment: Asserts LosslessTo refuses I64 to F32 (max int value far
exceeds F32 mantissa exact-integer ceiling). Pairs with the
I32 to F64 + U8 to F32 positive cases in Test.Lossless.

invocations.name: Run coverage gap probe (advisory)
comment: C backend FFI tests per available backend, via the Criterion
harness under `packages/backends/test/`. Per-OS: tape everywhere,
torch on Ubuntu (libtorch installed via uv), mlx on macOS
(MLX_SITE set above). The legacy `test_backend.c` monolith was
retired with the Criterion port — every assertion lives under
`test/common/test_legacy_backend.c` for now, slated for a
per-op file split during the structural Phase 6 work.
Static probe: parses OP_* enums from backend_<b>/tape.h and
extern "C" decls from backend.h, cross-references against
test/. Writes CSVs to build/coverage-gap-{ops,symbols}.csv.
Exit code is advisory today (0 even on gaps); coverage-policy.md
flips this to gating once W3+W4 close. See
docs/develop/coverage-policy.md for the three-axis target.

invocations.name: Run Idris unit suite (tape)
comment: Idris-side smart-constructor / LayerLike / Tensor-lifecycle suite
against the tape primary. The test buckets that touch the C
surface (GradMode, ManagedHandle) use `{d=TestDevice}` which the
Makefile-generated `TestConfig.idr` resolves to TapeDev here, so
FFI calls land on tape-suffixed C symbols.

invocations.name: Run Idris unit suite (torch, Ubuntu)
comment: Same suite as the tape lane but with TestDevice = TorchDev TCpu.
Catches Idris-side regressions that a tape-only run would miss
(broken torch Scheme wrapper, drift in `UserDeviceTransfer`
instances, etc.).

invocations.name: Run Idris unit suite (mlx, macOS)
comment: Same suite as tape/torch but with TestDevice = MlxDev MCpu.
Catches mlx Scheme-wrapper drift, lazy-eval / handle-lifetime
regressions in the test-managed-handle suite under Metal.

invocations.name: Run multi-backend Idris suite (macOS)
comment: Adds Test.Transfer (cross-backend `toDevice` smoke) +
Test.MultiDeviceRegistry (registry isolation invariant) on
top of the per-backend buckets. Forces BACKEND=torch,tape,mlx
so all three sets of C symbols are linked — only feasible on
the macOS lane (Ubuntu has no mlx).

invocations.name: Run safetensors round-trip (tape)
comment: F32/F64 param + optimizer-state round-trip; runs on every OS.
Re-installs the tape dylib so subsequent steps that expect
tape symbols (test-e2e-examples default lane) see them.

invocations.name: Run safetensors round-trip (torch, Ubuntu)
comment: Adds the bf16/f16/i32 byte-level round-trip (those dtypes exist
only on torch). Gated to the libtorch lane.

invocations.name: Run typed index-op round-trip (torch, Ubuntu)
comment: Verifies the typed targsort/tgather/tscatterAdd surface *resolves*
on torch (Compatible d I64) and runs — the C test covers numerics,
check-all is tape-only and can't resolve the I64 gate. Torch-only:
an integer-dtyped index tensor exists nowhere else.

invocations.name: Run integration tests
comment: No SKIP_EXAMPLES: the mlx allocator aborts that used to skip
ntm-copy / ntm-associative-recall / dnc-recall / mountain-car-cont
are fixed by the generation-scoped free (see
docs/develop/tensor-lifecycle.md). The whole matrix runs.

invocations.name: Checkpoint resume smoke test
comment: Trains gpt 10 epochs to a checkpoint dir, resumes to 20, and
asserts the sidecar epoch + resume log + completion. Gates the
Train.idr / Checkpoint.idr auto-save / resume integration.
